proposals: P25 - BC-07's and the renderer's lowercase-word patterns disagree about hyphens, so BC-07 demands a spelling renderer.canonical() is forbidden to write. Measured on run 1's own rendered prose: the validator's (?<![.\w])[a-z]{3,}\b matches 'pdf' 7 times and yields violation ['pdf']; the renderer's (?<![.\w:-])[a-z]{3,}(?![\w:-]) matches it 0 times and yields []. All 7 sit inside hyphenated tokens - 6 in the module path aspose-pdf-foss/aspose-pdf-foss-for-go, 1 in the upstream ticket slug '(epic pdf-go-w4ht)'. The failure carries section_id null, so no repair is attempted. P19's shape one check over, and arrival item 26's reasoning for BC-08 one check over. Fix: give validation/registry.py's _LOWER_WORD the renderer's hyphen guard. Proven on this candidate's bytes: 7 matches to 0, one violation to none. Trade-off stated plainly: that guard also stops BC-07 seeing a violation someone might genuinely write in prose ("the pdf-format output"). The narrower alternative is to exempt only a lowercase abbreviation falling inside a SUPPORTED fact value and keep failing it elsewhere - more faithful, more code. Either way the invariant is the one that matters: BC-07 must not demand a spelling renderer.canonical() is forbidden to write, and the check and the normaliser should be built from one pattern rather than two that drifted apart.

P26 - a Go module path is one identifier and the renderer splits it. identifier_tokens() has _COORDINATE for a colon-bearing Maven coordinate but nothing for a slash-bearing Go module path: identifier_tokens('... and Save methods from github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/aspose-pdf-foss-for-go.') returns ['github.com'] only. renderer.prose therefore renders '`github.com`/aspose-pdf-foss/aspose-pdf-foss-for-go' - a split identifier in the visible README, which loop-prompt.md section 6 rule 8 names a defect in its own right. Three units carry it. Measured as NOT sufficient for BC-07 on its own: wrapping the path takes the 'pdf' matches from 7 to 1, and the survivor '(epic pdf-go-w4ht)' is ordinary prose. P25 is the necessary fix; P26 removes the split identifier.

P27 - a link probe that times out is never asked again. 091e8bc gave registry probes a retry for every ecosystem; link probes have none. One ReadTimeout at 32,662 ms turned a link that answers 200 in about a second into UNRESOLVED and failed BC-06 at EXTRACTING. Evidence: three independent live GETs at 200 in 2,362 / 701 / 764 ms, and run 2's production probe at RESOLVED 200 in 1,028 ms, all at the same revision within twenty minutes.

P28 - a check's repairability is decided by its worst failure, not per failure. repair/targeted.py::validation_defects reads check['causal_stage'], one value for the whole check, and only then, and only for stage S6, looks at per-failure section_id. BC-06 carried an EXTRACTING and a COMPOSING failure together; the check-level value was EXTRACTING, so the COMPOSING failure carrying section_id 'additional_examples' was never considered. This is exactly what stopped item 47 - landed for this repository by name - from being exercised in run 1.

P29 - S5 planning truncates at its 6,000-token budget on a coin flip, and the body that would explain it is discarded. Proven on one request digest: calls.jsonl records presentation_planning req 8be652cfcbc2 returning 6,000 completion tokens with finish_reason length (run 2, transaction killed six stages before validation) and the SAME digest returning 3,351 completion tokens cleanly (run 3); run 1's slightly different request da3aac42f740 returned 2,102. Nothing about the packet changed - the digest is the proof. prompts/presentation_planning.yaml sets max_output_tokens 6000 and bounds core_capabilities (3-8), api_hubs (<=12) and capability_titles (3-8), but leaves sections, additional_example_ids, material_limitations, links, deviations and every nested fact_ids/shared_fact_ids/unit_ids/input_format_ids/output_format_ids array with no maxItems; composition/planning.py pins those arrays' items to citable_fact_ids() as one enum (3e9b81f) but not their length, and this repository's citable set is 512 values - P23's residual one stage over, where the batch no longer bounds the count. NOT PROVEN that this truncation was a runaway array, and that is the second half of the proposal: core/llm/jobs.py's finish_reason == 'length' branch calls attempts.record_invalid() and raises without calling store.reject(), so reply.content is discarded, though CallStore.reject's own docstring is 'Keep a rejected reply beside the store, so a rejection can be read, never guessed.' Fix, smallest first: store the truncated body like any other rejection; then bound the five unbounded arrays, as authoring_schema() already bounds its slots. Raising the budget alone moves the ceiling.

P30 - the anchor is in a preserved unit and the repair may only edit authored ones. Measured in run 3: repairs.json's single change is before == after ('Create encrypted documents, build tables with the Rectangle API, and render pages to images.') at path units.0.text, the additional_examples authored 'preview' slot, which carries no anchor; the anchor is in inherited_unit:025.paragraph, VERIFIED_PRESERVE into the same section, at README.md line 223. The repairer was shown the right section and handed the only units it may edit, none of which is the one carrying the defect, so it returned the text unchanged, the round was recorded as 'repaired', and BC-06 re-raised on the identical detail. This is the cause half PROPOSAL P20 named: 'a preserved unit's intra-document anchor should be resolved against the planned headings when the unit is placed - rewritten to the heading that survived, or dropped to plain text - rather than carried into the document to fail at S9.' Placement is the right place: at S4/S5 the planned headings are known and an anchor resolving to none of them can be downgraded to its link text deterministically, with no provider call. Repairing it at S6 cannot work while preserved units sit outside the repair's edit surface. Corroboration, not a new class: a repair writing back byte-identical prose is still recorded as 'repaired' with a re-raise rather than as a no-op - RERUN3 saw the same shape on 2026-09-06 and named lane C's item 34; this is a second, independent occurrence in a different ecosystem.
